title: Lubricant Task Group Final Report
subtitle: Steel Coalition Lubricant Task Group — Final Report · May 14, 2002
organization: AISI · MBMA · MCA · NCCA · SDI · SJI
citation: Steel Coalition (2002), Lubricant Task Group Final Report

background.heading: BACKGROUND · Sec. 1
background.body: OSHA Subpart R rulemaking targets slip-and-fall injuries in steel erection; Sotter (1998) identifies jobsite lubricants on deck/roofing as a slipping hazard — Task Group formed to reduce or eliminate lubricants on as-delivered product.

branches.title: Stack Tests
branches.subtitle: (Storage Stain)
bullets: Only SLS-54 (Grp C) resists white rust

items.label: Group A
items.text: 100% volatile organic solvents; no residue; evaporate in 2–15 min

items.label: Group B
items.text: >95% volatile solvents + <5% lubricity additives; trace residue, hard to detect

items.label: Group C
items.text: partially volatile "slushing/vanishing oils" with rust inhibitors; oily residue remains

items.label: Group D
items.text: water-soluble, oil-free; small residue that re-dissolves when wetted

items.label: Group E
items.text: oil-in-water emulsion with inhibitor; small oily residue, re-emulsifies

synopsis.heading: SYNOPSIS OF EVALUATIONS · Sec. 3
synopsis.body: Lubrication is unavoidable for bare metallic-coated sheet, but low/no-residue forming is feasible; "vanishing oil" terminology is misleading and inconsistent; storage-stain protection needs either chemical passivation or Group C oils; acrylic-coated sheet forms dry without lubricant.

bullets: Each manufacturer sets its own parameters; safety/environmental compliance is local
Prefer highly evaporative (>95% volatile) forming lubricants where possible
Retire the term "vanishing oil" — use "Evaporative Compound" vs. "Corrosion Inhibiting Lubricant"

groups.label: Roofing panels:
bullets: Acrylic-coated or dry chem-treated coils first; Group C only discretely, low-slope + labels

groups.label: Deck products:
bullets: Order dry / painted / oil-free coils when possible
In plant: highly evaporative rolling lubricants, controlled application; none on painted product

outcome.heading: OUTCOME
outcome.body: Industry evaluates recommendations in-plant for two years, then final recommendations go to OSHA; Coalition monitors and shares findings.
